searches.reason: Develop paired sequence interventions—recent-history truncation, removal of repeated interests, and order shuffling—to test whether recommendations depend on supported recent behavior. Measure score and rank changes against matched random-removal controls, then connect failures to sequence encoding, positional attention, and training objectives. Treat perturbation sensitivity as a diagnostic association, not proof of causal user preference.

searches.reason: Replace reliance on raw training margins with trustworthy ranking diagnostics: compare uniform, popularity-matched, and hard negatives; stratify by dataset, item popularity, and history length; and estimate uncertainty with paired user bootstrap intervals. Investigate whether these probes predict the pinned validation HR@10 and agree with full-catalog unseen-item rankings for the twenty feedback users, while keeping the host evaluator unchanged.

searches.reason: Build feedback-grounded probes for direct versus adjacent relevance, explicit compatibility conflicts, and redundant recommendations using only histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions. Seek evidence extraction with an explicit insufficient-information outcome and human calibration. Do not infer unmet need, satisfaction, ownership, or simulator traits from interaction history alone; sparse metadata should reduce coverage rather than produce invented mismatch labels.
